```{r}
# Function to calculate weighted mean and propagated error
# 1) For library-overlapping data
calculate_weighted_mean_and_error <- function(
  df,
  col1,
  column_fitness,
  column_sigma,
  weighted_mean_col,
  propagated_error_col
) {

  df %>%
    dplyr::group_by_at(
      col1
    ) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(

      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::everything(),
        ~ .x[1],
        .names = "{.col}"
      ),

      !!rlang::sym(weighted_mean_col) :=
        sum(
          (!!rlang::sym(column_fitness)) /
            (!!rlang::sym(column_sigma))^2,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ) /
        sum(
          1 /
            (!!rlang::sym(column_sigma))^2,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      !!rlang::sym(propagated_error_col) :=
        sqrt(
          1 /
            sum(
              1 /
                (!!rlang::sym(column_sigma))^2,
              na.rm = TRUE
            )
        ),

      .groups = "drop"
    )
}



# Function to calculate Weighted.mean and pass error 
# 2) For getting fitness data of unique AA mut
calculate_unique_weighted_mean_and_error <- function(
  df,
  col1,
  column_fitness,
  column_sigma,
  weighted_mean_col,
  propagated_error_col
) {

  df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(col1)
      )
    ) %>%

    dplyr::mutate(

      !!rlang::sym(weighted_mean_col) :=

        if (dplyr::n() == 1) {

          .data[[column_fitness]]

        } else {

          sum(
            .data[[column_fitness]] /
              .data[[column_sigma]]^2,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ) /
            sum(
              1 /
                .data[[column_sigma]]^2,
              na.rm = TRUE
            )
        },


      !!rlang::sym(propagated_error_col) :=

        if (dplyr::n() == 1) {

          .data[[column_sigma]]

        } else {

          sqrt(
            1 /
              sum(
                1 /
                  .data[[column_sigma]]^2,
                na.rm = TRUE
              )
          )
        }
    ) %>%

    dplyr::ungroup()
}



# Function to supplement annotations at genome nt level based on the position 1 of mutations
update_genome_nt_positions <- function(
  df,
  pos_col = "genome_nt_mut_pos1"
) {

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Check input
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (!pos_col %in% names(df)) {
    stop(
      "Position column not found: ",
      pos_col
    )
  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Define genomic ranges
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  noncoding_ranges <- list(
    c(965, 1000),
    c(2285, 2394),
    c(2923, 2930),
    c(3918, 3980)
  )


  coding_ranges <- list(
    c(1, 964),
    c(1001, 2284),
    c(2395, 2922),
    c(2931, 3917),
    c(3981, 5386)
  )


  overlap_orf_ranges <- list(
    c(1, 221),
    c(390, 393),
    c(568, 843),
    c(848, 848),
    c(5075, 5386)
  )


  structural_ranges <- list(
    c(1, 51),
    c(390, 964),
    c(1001, 2284),
    c(2395, 2922),
    c(5075, 5386)
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: vectorized test for whether positions fall in any
  # of the supplied ranges
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  is_in_ranges <- function(x, ranges) {

    result <-
      Reduce(
        `|`,
        lapply(
          ranges,
          function(r) {
            x >= r[1] &
              x <= r[2]
          }
        )
      )

    result[
      is.na(x)
    ] <-
      NA

    result
  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Annotate
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  pos <-
    df[[pos_col]]


  df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      genome_nt_pos_noncoding =
        dplyr::if_else(
          is_in_ranges(
            pos,
            noncoding_ranges
          ),
          "Noncoding",
          NA_character_,
          missing = NA_character_
        ),

      genome_nt_pos_coding =
        dplyr::if_else(
          is_in_ranges(
            pos,
            coding_ranges
          ),
          "Coding",
          NA_character_,
          missing = NA_character_
        ),

      genome_nt_pos_overlap_orf =
        dplyr::if_else(
          is_in_ranges(
            pos,
            overlap_orf_ranges
          ),
          "Overlapping Coding",
          NA_character_,
          missing = NA_character_
        ),

      genome_nt_pos_structural =
        is_in_ranges(
          pos,
          structural_ranges
        )
    )
}
```

```{r}
## Function to compute p-value for Statitic tests
# Two-samples t-test
two_samples_ttest <- function(mu1, sem1, n1, mu2, sem2, n2) {
  # Compute t-statistic using SEM directly
  t_stat <- (mu1 - mu2) / sqrt(sem1^2 + sem2^2)

  # Compute degrees of freedom (Welch’s approximation)
  df <- (sem1^2 + sem2^2)^2 /
        ((sem1^4 / (n1 - 1)) + (sem2^4 / (n2 - 1)))

  # Ensure df is valid
  if (is.na(df) || df <= 0) {
    df <- 1  # Prevent invalid df values
  }

  # Compute two-tailed p-value
  p_val <- 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stat), df))

  return(p_val)
}



# Function for mutation category and direction, using Increased, No effect, Detrimental, Strongly detrimental four classes
assign_mutation_categories_fdr <- function(
  df,
  pval_col,
  effect_raw_col,
  alpha = 0.05,
  effect_breaks = c(0.10, 0.15, 0.50),

  effect_bin_col,
  category_fdr_col,
  category_fdr_lethal_col,
  category_cutoff_col,
  category_combined_col,

  direction_col,
  direction_lethal_col
) {

  # ============================================================
  # Checks
  # ============================================================

  required_cols <- c(
    pval_col,
    effect_raw_col
  )

  missing_cols <-
    setdiff(
      required_cols,
      names(df)
    )

  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop(
      "Missing required columns: ",
      paste(
        missing_cols,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  }

  if (!is.numeric(effect_breaks)) {
    stop(
      "effect_breaks must be numeric."
    )
  }

  if (length(effect_breaks) != 3) {
    stop(
      "effect_breaks should contain three values, ",
      "e.g. c(0.10, 0.15, 0.50)."
    )
  }

  effect_breaks <-
    sort(
      effect_breaks
    )


  # ============================================================
  # Extract numeric vectors
  # ============================================================

  p <-
    as.numeric(
      df[[pval_col]]
    )

  e <-
    as.numeric(
      df[[effect_raw_col]]
    )


  # ============================================================
  # Statistical significance
  # ============================================================

  sig_flag <-
    !is.na(p) &
    p < alpha


  # ============================================================
  # Primary FDR-based classification
  #
  # Revised terminology:
  # Increased
  # No effect
  # Detrimental
  # ============================================================

  category_fdr <-
    dplyr::case_when(

      is.na(p) |
        is.na(e) ~
        NA_character_,

      !sig_flag ~
        "No effect",

      e > 0 ~
        "Increased",

      e < 0 ~
        "Detrimental",

      TRUE ~
        "No effect"
    )


  # ============================================================
  # Effect-size bins
  #
  # Only statistically significant variants are assigned
  # non-zero effect-size bins.
  # ============================================================

  effect_bin_num <-
    dplyr::case_when(

      is.na(e) ~
        NA_real_,

      !sig_flag ~
        0,

      abs(e) >= effect_breaks[3] ~
        effect_breaks[3],

      abs(e) >= effect_breaks[2] ~
        effect_breaks[2],

      abs(e) >= effect_breaks[1] ~
        effect_breaks[1],

      TRUE ~
        0
    )


  # ============================================================
  # Strongly detrimental refinement
  #
  # Historical output column name is retained for compatibility,
  # but "Lethal" is no longer used as a category.
  # ============================================================

  category_fdr_lethal <-
    dplyr::case_when(

      is.na(category_fdr) ~
        NA_character_,

      category_fdr ==
        "Detrimental" &
        effect_bin_num >= effect_breaks[3] ~
        "Strongly detrimental",

      TRUE ~
        category_fdr
    )


  # ============================================================
  # Effect-size cutoff refinement
  #
  # Statistically significant effects smaller than the middle
  # cutoff are reassigned to "No measurable effect".
  # ============================================================

  category_cutoff <-
    dplyr::case_when(

      is.na(category_fdr) ~
        NA_character_,

      category_fdr %in%
        c(
          "Increased",
          "Detrimental"
        ) &
        effect_bin_num < effect_breaks[2] ~
        "No effect",

      category_fdr ==
        "Detrimental" &
        effect_bin_num >= effect_breaks[3] ~
        "Strongly detrimental",

      TRUE ~
        category_fdr
    )


  # ============================================================
  # Two-class combined classification
  # ============================================================

  category_combined <-
    dplyr::case_when(

      category_cutoff %in%
        c(
          "Increased",
          "No effect"
        ) ~
        "No reduced replication",

      category_cutoff %in%
        c(
          "Detrimental",
          "Strongly detrimental"
        ) ~
        "Reduced replication",

      TRUE ~
        NA_character_
    )


  # ============================================================
  # Direction without strong-effect subdivision
  #
  # Column name is retained, but terminology is replication-based.
  # ============================================================

  direction <-
    dplyr::case_when(

      is.na(category_fdr) ~
        NA_character_,

      category_fdr ==
        "Increased" ~
        "Increased replication",

      category_fdr ==
        "No effect" ~
        "No measurable effect",

      category_fdr ==
        "Detrimental" ~
        "Reduced replication",

      TRUE ~
        NA_character_
    )


  # ============================================================
  # Direction including strongly detrimental category
  #
  # Historical output column name is retained for compatibility.
  # ============================================================

  direction_lethal <-
    dplyr::case_when(

      is.na(category_fdr_lethal) ~
        NA_character_,

      category_fdr_lethal ==
        "Increased" ~
        "Increased replication",

      category_fdr_lethal ==
        "No effect" ~
        "No measurable effect",

      category_fdr_lethal ==
        "Detrimental" ~
        "Reduced replication",

      category_fdr_lethal ==
        "Strongly detrimental" ~
        "Strongly reduced replication",

      TRUE ~
        NA_character_
    )


  # ============================================================
  # Safe overwrite of existing output columns
  # ============================================================

  output_cols <- c(
    effect_bin_col,
    category_fdr_col,
    category_fdr_lethal_col,
    category_cutoff_col,
    category_combined_col,
    direction_col,
    direction_lethal_col
  )

  for (col in output_cols) {
    df[[col]] <- NULL
  }


  # ============================================================
  # Assign outputs
  # ============================================================

  df[[effect_bin_col]] <-
    factor(
      effect_bin_num,
      levels = c(
        0,
        effect_breaks
      )
    )


  df[[category_fdr_col]] <-
    factor(
      category_fdr,
      levels = c(
        "Increased",
        "No effect",
        "Detrimental"
      )
    )


  df[[category_fdr_lethal_col]] <-
    factor(
      category_fdr_lethal,
      levels = c(
        "Increased",
        "No effect",
        "Detrimental",
        "Strongly detrimental"
      )
    )


  df[[category_cutoff_col]] <-
    factor(
      category_cutoff,
      levels = c(
        "Increased",
        "No effect",
        "Detrimental",
        "Strongly detrimental"
      )
    )


  df[[category_combined_col]] <-
    factor(
      category_combined,
      levels = c(
        "No reduced replication",
        "Reduced replication"
      )
    )


  df[[direction_col]] <-
    factor(
      direction,
      levels = c(
        "Increased replication",
        "No measurable effect",
        "Reduced replication"
      )
    )


  df[[direction_lethal_col]] <-
    factor(
      direction_lethal,
      levels = c(
        "Increased replication",
        "No measurable effect",
        "Reduced replication",
        "Strongly reduced replication"
      )
    )


  return(df)
}
```

```{r}
# Function to generate summary table
generate_mutation_category_summary <- function(
    df, 
    class_col,
    category_col,
    total_count = NULL
) {

  class_syms    <- rlang::syms(class_col)
  category_sym  <- rlang::ensym(category_col)

  df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(!!category_sym)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(!!!class_syms, !!category_sym) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(count = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(!!!class_syms) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      proportion = if (is.null(total_count)) {
        count / sum(count)
      } else {
        count / total_count
      },
      percent = round(proportion * 100, 2)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
}



# Function to plot the correlation across bio-replicates
plot_replicate_reproducibility <- function(df,
                                           replicate_cols,
                                           cor_method = "pearson",
                                           point_alpha = 0.5,
                                           point_size = 1.2,
                                           title = "Reproducibility Across Replicates") {
  # ---- Check inputs ----
  stopifnot(all(replicate_cols %in% names(df)))
  
  # ---- Load required library ----
  if (!requireNamespace("GGally", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Please install 'GGally' package: install.packages('GGally')")
  }

  # ---- Subset and clean data ----
  df_sub <- df[, replicate_cols]
  df_sub <- df_sub[stats::complete.cases(df_sub), ]

  # ---- Build ggpairs plot ----
  p <- ggpairs(
    df_sub,
    upper = list(continuous = wrap("cor",
                                           size = 4,
                                           method = cor_method,
                                           use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
                                           color = "black")),
    lower = list(continuous = wrap("points",
                                           alpha = point_alpha,
                                           size = point_size,
                                           color = "black")),
                                           #color = "gray88")),
    diag = list(continuous = wrap("densityDiag",
                                          alpha = 0.6,
                                          fill = "gray88"))
  ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    ggtitle(title)

  return(p)
}



# Function - Pir charts
plot_pie_summary <- function(data, 
                              x_col = "Var1", 
                              y_col = "Freq", 
                              plot_title = NULL,
                              outline_color = "black",
                              outline_linewidth = 0.6,
                              palette = "Set3",
                              remove_legend = FALSE,
                              show_text = TRUE) {    
  
  x_sym <- rlang::sym(x_col)
  y_sym <- rlang::sym(y_col)

  # Prepare and order the data by descending y_col
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(
      percentage = round(100 * !!y_sym / sum(!!y_sym), 1),
      legend_label = paste0(!!x_sym, " (", percentage, "%)")
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(!!y_sym)) %>%
    mutate(
      legend_label = factor(legend_label, levels = unique(legend_label)),  # Order legend
      fraction = !!y_sym / sum(!!y_sym),
      ymax = cumsum(fraction),
      ymin = c(0, head(ymax, -1))
    )

  p <- ggplot(data) +
    geom_rect(
      aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, xmin = 0.5, xmax = 1.5, fill = legend_label),
      color = outline_color,
      linewidth = outline_linewidth
    ) +
    coord_polar(theta = "y") +
    xlim(0.5, 2.2) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(title = plot_title, fill = NULL) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = palette) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
    )
  
  # Add text if requested
  if (show_text) {
    p <- p + geom_text(
      aes(x = 1, y = (ymin + ymax) / 2, label = paste0(percentage, "%")),
      size = 5,
      color = "black"
    )
  }

  # Optionally remove legend
  if (remove_legend) {
    p <- p + theme(legend.position = "none")
  }
  
  return(p)
}



# Function to plot ridgeline plot
plot_ridgeline_mut_class <- function(data,
                                     score_col = fitness_final,
                                     class_col = phix_aa_mut_class,
                                     plot_title = "Ridgeline Density Plot of Fitness Final",
                                     x_label = "Fitness") {
  
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = {{ score_col }}, y = {{ class_col }})) +
    geom_density_ridges(
      scale = 1.2,
      fill = "grey88",
      color = "black",
      alpha = 0.8
    ) +
    xlim(-1, 1.5) +
    labs(
      title = plot_title,
      x = x_label,
      y = "Mutation Class"
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
  
  return(p)
}
```

## Statistics
t-test and FDR: two-sample t-test, compare to Synonymous distribution as the reference (for 1nt variants, separately);

1) 1nt Data
  Syn final fitness: phix_1nt_synonymous_combined_fitness_final
  Syn final sigma: phix_1nt_synonymous_combined_sigma_final
2) AA Data
  Syn final fitness: phix_all_synonymous_combined_fitness_final
  Syn final sigma: phix_all_synonymous_combined_sigma_final

### 1) Get Reference data (Synonymous)
Filter the synonymous fitness (normalized final) data, and calculate weighted.mean and propagate the error of SEM and make sure data is filtered correctly and remove NA values

```{r}
## All variants
filtered_data_all_synonymous <- phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique %>%
  filter(phix_aa_mut_class == "Synonymous", !is.na(fitness_final))

# get weighted.mean of all synonymous mutations;
phix_all_synonymous_combined_weights <- 1 / (filtered_data_all_synonymous$sigma_final^2)  # Weights are the inverse of variance
phix_all_synonymous_combined_fitness_final <- sum(filtered_data_all_synonymous$fitness_final * phix_all_synonymous_combined_weights) / sum(phix_all_synonymous_combined_weights) 
# [1] 0.9807827
phix_all_synonymous_combined_sigma_final <- sqrt(1/sum(phix_all_synonymous_combined_weights)) 
# [1] 0.0002573693



## 1nt variants
filtered_data_1nt_synonymous <- phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique %>%
  filter(genome_nt_mut_ham == 1, phix_aa_mut_class == "Synonymous", !is.na(fitness_final))

# get weighted.mean of all 1nt synonymous mutations;
phix_1nt_synonymous_combined_weights <- 1 / (filtered_data_1nt_synonymous$sigma_final^2)  # Weights are the inverse of variance
phix_1nt_synonymous_combined_fitness_final <- sum(filtered_data_1nt_synonymous$fitness_final * phix_1nt_synonymous_combined_weights) / sum(phix_1nt_synonymous_combined_weights) 
# [1] 0.978221
phix_1nt_synonymous_combined_sigma_final <- sqrt(1/sum(phix_1nt_synonymous_combined_weights)) # Sigma final = 0.0002678072, 0.0002678328, 0.0002812053
# [1] 0.0002813241



```


### 2) two-sample t-tests
```{r}
# Make a copy for statistics
phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat <- phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique


# Apply the function row-wise, the sample size is related to how many nt muts are merged to one AA mut 
phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat$p_value_two_sample_ttest_syn <- mapply(
  two_samples_ttest,
  phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat$fitness_final,  # mu1 (row-wise)
  phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat$sigma_final,    # sem1 (row-wise)
  MoreArgs = list(
    n1 = 3,  # Fixed (n1),
    mu2 = phix_all_synonymous_combined_fitness_final,  # Fixed (mu2)
    sem2 = phix_all_synonymous_combined_sigma_final,   # Fixed (sem2)
    n2 = 3  # Fixed (n2)
  )
)


# Apply FDR correction using the function p.adjust() from basic R;
phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat <- phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat %>%
  mutate(p_value_two_sample_ttest_syn_FDR = p.adjust(p_value_two_sample_ttest_syn, method = "BH"))


# Add raw effect size (difference from the synonymous baseline)
phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat$effect_size_vs_syn <-
  phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat$fitness_final -
  phix_all_synonymous_combined_fitness_final


# Add standardized effect (signal-to-noise; same scaling as t-stat numerator)
phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat$effect_size_std_vs_syn <-
  (phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat$fitness_final -
   phix_all_synonymous_combined_fitness_final) /
  sqrt(phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat$sigma_final^2 +
       phix_all_synonymous_combined_sigma_final^2)



```


### 3) Mutation Category
Updated FUNCTION: assign_mutation_categories_fdr
```{r}

  phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat,
  pval_col = "p_value_two_sample_ttest_syn_FDR",
  effect_raw_col = "effect_size_vs_syn",
  
  alpha = 0.05,
  effect_breaks = c(0.10, 0.15, 0.50),

  # Output column names
  effect_bin_col = "effect_size_bin",
  category_fdr_col = "mutation_category_FDR",
  category_fdr_lethal_col = "mutation_category_FDR_lethal",
  category_cutoff_col = "mutation_category_FDR_cutoff",
  category_combined_col = "mutation_category_FDR_cutoff_combined",
  
  direction_col = "mutation_direction",
  direction_lethal_col = "mutation_direction_lethal"
)
```

### 4) Complete nucleotides annotations
separate noncoding annotations to the all sub data data.frame
- RBS, Promoters, Terminators, Ori+ ... 

```{r}
# Supplement annotations
phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat <-
  phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat %>%
  
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    # ---- 1) nucleotide class priority ----
    genome_nt_pos_nucleotide_class = purrr::pmap_chr(
      list(genome_nt_pos_overlap_orf, genome_nt_pos_coding, genome_nt_pos_noncoding),
      ~ {
        if (!is.na(..1)) {
          as.character(..1)
        } else if (!is.na(..2)) {
          as.character(..2)
        } else if (!is.na(..3)) {
          as.character(..3)
        } else {
          NA_character_
        }
      }
    )
  ) %>%

  # ---- RBS ----
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tibble(
      genome_nt_mut_pos1 = c(
        5063:5068, 39:45, 124:130, 378:381, 555:558,
        836:840, 991:994, 2383:2387, 2923:2928, 3969:3973
      ),
      genome_nt_pos_RBS = "RBS",
      genome_nt_pos_RBS_gene = c(
        rep("RBS (B)", length(5063:5068)),
        rep("RBS (K)", length(39:45)),
        rep("RBS (C)", length(124:130)),
        rep("RBS (D)", length(378:381)),
        rep("RBS (E)", length(555:558)),
        rep("RBS (J)", length(836:840)),
        rep("RBS (F)", length(991:994)),
        rep("RBS (G)", length(2383:2387)),
        rep("RBS (H)", length(2923:2928)),
        rep("RBS (A)", length(3969:3973))
      )
    ),
    by = "genome_nt_mut_pos1"
  ) %>%

  # ---- promoter ----
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tibble(
      genome_nt_mut_pos1 = c(3927:3955, 129:155, 4863:4892, 313:357),
      genome_nt_pos_promoter = "Promoter",
      genome_nt_pos_promoter_gene = c(
        rep("pA", length(3927:3955)),
        rep("pD2 (btss49)", length(129:155)),
        rep("pB", length(4863:4892)),
        rep("pD", length(313:357))
      )
    ),
    by = "genome_nt_mut_pos1"
  ) %>%

  # ---- anti-sense promoter ----
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tibble(
      genome_nt_mut_pos1 = c(2753:2779, 4021:4052),
      genome_nt_pos_promoter_anti_sense = c(
        rep("pR3", length(2753:2779)),
        rep("pR12", length(4021:4052))
      )
    ),
    by = "genome_nt_mut_pos1"
  ) %>%

  # ---- terminator ----
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tibble(
      genome_nt_mut_pos1 = c(3956:3974, 2909:2942, 5160:5238, 2308:2351, 969:985),
      genome_nt_pos_terminator = "Terminator",
      genome_nt_pos_terminator_gene = c(
        rep("TH", length(3956:3974)),
        rep("TG", length(2909:2942)),
        rep("TB (RUT-3)", length(5160:5238)),
        rep("TF", length(2308:2351)),
        rep("TJ", length(969:985))
      )
    ),
    by = "genome_nt_mut_pos1"
  ) %>%

  dplyr::mutate(
    
    # ---- ORI ----
    genome_nt_pos_ori = dplyr::case_when(
      genome_nt_mut_ham == 1 &
        genome_nt_mut_pos1 %in% c(4299:4328) ~ "Ori (+)",
        genome_nt_mut_pos1 %in% c(2308:2351) ~ "Ori (-)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    # ---- combine annotations ----
    genome_nt_pos_annotation = purrr::pmap_chr(
      list(
        genome_nt_pos_RBS,
        genome_nt_pos_promoter,
        genome_nt_pos_terminator,
        genome_nt_pos_ori,
        genome_nt_mut_pos1
      ),
      ~ {
        values <- na.omit(c(..1, ..2, ..3, ..4))
        
        if (length(values) == 0 &&
            ..5 %in% c(965:1000, 2285:2394, 2923:2930, 3918:3980)) {
          "Unknown Noncoding"
        } else if (length(values) == 0) {
          NA_character_
        } else {
          paste(unique(values), collapse = ",")
        }
      }
    )
  )

table(phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat$genome_nt_pos_annotation)
```

```{r}

  filter(genome_nt_pos_coding == "Coding") 


# Check the frequency of each mut ID, and supplement aa mut frequency and Sample size to the data.frame

  merge(phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_aa, count_table_phix_aa_mut_ID, by = "phix_aa_mut_ID")

phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_aa$phix_aa_mut_ID_sample_size <- 
  phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_aa$phix_aa_mut_ID_freq*3

# Calculate fitness for unique genotypes by weighte.mean for the same phix_aa_mut_ID

  phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_aa,

)
```

```{r}
#      36081        2542         339        1396 

#   Missense   Nonsense  Stop-loss Synonymous 
#      36074       2542        345       1396 


# Get AA-level reference
filtered_data_AA_synonymous <- phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_AA %>%
  filter(phix_aa_mut_class == "Synonymous", !is.na(fitness_final_unique))

# get weighted.mean of all 1nt synonymous mutations;
phix_AA_synonymous_combined_weights <- 1 / (filtered_data_AA_synonymous$sigma_final^2)  # Weights are the inverse of variance
phix_AA_synonymous_combined_fitness_final <- sum(filtered_data_AA_synonymous$fitness_final * phix_AA_synonymous_combined_weights) / sum(phix_AA_synonymous_combined_weights) 
# [1] 0.9779537
phix_AA_synonymous_combined_sigma_final <- sqrt(1/sum(phix_AA_synonymous_combined_weights)) 
# [1] 0.0004107135


# Apply the function row-wise, the sample size is related to how many nt muts are merged to one AA mut 
phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_AA$p_value_AA_two_sample_ttest_syn <- mapply(
  two_samples_ttest,
  phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_AA$fitness_final_unique,  # mu1 (row-wise)
  phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_AA$sigma_final_unique,    # sem1 (row-wise)
  MoreArgs = list(
    n1 = 3,  # Fixed (n1),
    mu2 = phix_AA_synonymous_combined_fitness_final,  # Fixed (mu2)
    sem2 = phix_AA_synonymous_combined_sigma_final,   # Fixed (sem2)
    n2 = 3  # Fixed (n2)
  )
)


# Apply FDR correction using the function p.adjust() from basic R;
phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_AA <- phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_AA %>%
  mutate(p_value_AA_two_sample_ttest_syn_FDR = p.adjust(p_value_AA_two_sample_ttest_syn, method = "BH"))


# Add raw effect size (difference from the synonymous baseline)
phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_AA$effect_size_vs_AA_syn <-
  phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_AA$fitness_final -
  phix_AA_synonymous_combined_fitness_final


# Add standardized effect (signal-to-noise; same scaling as t-stat numerator)
phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_AA$effect_size_std_vs_AA_syn <-
  (phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_AA$fitness_final -
   phix_AA_synonymous_combined_fitness_final) /
  sqrt(phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_AA$sigma_final^2 +
       phix_AA_synonymous_combined_sigma_final^2)



```

### 4) Volcano plots (Statistics)
Fitness effects and statistical significance
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Updated volcano plots
# ============================================================
replication_category_colors <- c(
  "Increased" = "#A1A9D0",
  "No effect"  = "#D9D9D9",
  "Detrimental"   = "#F4A6A6",
  "Strongly detrimental"  = "#F0988C"
)

replication_category_levels <- c(
  "Increased",
  "No effect",
  "Detrimental",
  "Strongly detrimental"
)

plot_volcano <- function(
  data,
  x_col = "fitness_final",
  y_col = "p_adj_two_samples_syn",
  color_col = "mutation_category_FDR_cutoff",
  x_lim = c(-1, 1.5),
  y_lim = c(0, 2.7),
  reference_value = 1,
  strong_effect_cutoff = 0.5,
  fdr_cutoff = 0.05,
  plot_title = "Volcano plot"
) {

  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Thresholds
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  strong_threshold <-
    reference_value -
    strong_effect_cutoff

  fdr_y <-
    -log10(
      fdr_cutoff
    )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Prepare plotting data
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  plot_data <-
    data %>%
    mutate(

      .x =
        as.numeric(
          .data[[x_col]]
        ),

      .p =
        as.numeric(
          .data[[y_col]]
        ),

      .y =
        -log10(
          pmax(
            .p,
            .Machine$double.xmin
          )
        ),

      .category =
        as.character(
          .data[[color_col]]
        ),

      # Convert historical terminology if still present
      .category =
        recode(
          .category,

          "Beneficial" =
            "Increased",

          "Increased replication" =
            "Increased",

          "Neutral" =
            "No effect",

          "No measurable effect" =
            "No effect",

          "Reduced replication" =
            "Detrimental",

          "Lethal" =
            "Strongly detrimental",

          "Strongly reduced replication" =
            "Strongly detrimental"
        ),

      .category =
        factor(
          .category,
          levels =
            replication_category_levels
        )
    )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Percentage of variants in each category
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  percentage_data <-
    plot_data %>%

    filter(
      !is.na(
        .category
      )
    ) %>%

    dplyr::count(
      .category,
      .drop = FALSE
    ) %>%

    mutate(
      percentage =
        100 *
        n /
        sum(n),

      label =
        sprintf(
          "%.1f%%",
          percentage
        )
    )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Positions of percentage labels
  #
  # Strongly detrimental : upper left
  # Detrimental          : upper middle
  # Increased            : upper right
  # No effect            : below FDR threshold
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  percentage_positions <-
    tibble::tibble(

      .category =
        factor(
          replication_category_levels,
          levels =
            replication_category_levels
        ),

      label_x =
        c(

          # Increased
          (
            reference_value +
              x_lim[2]
          ) / 2,

          # No effect
          x_lim[1] +
            0.12 *
            diff(
              x_lim
            ),

          # Detrimental
          (
            strong_threshold +
              reference_value
          ) / 2,

          # Strongly detrimental
          (
            x_lim[1] +
              strong_threshold
          ) / 2
        ),

      label_y =
        c(

          # Increased
          y_lim[2] -
            0.18,

          # No effect
          fdr_y *
            0.35,

          # Detrimental
          y_lim[2] -
            0.18,

          # Strongly detrimental
          y_lim[2] -
            0.18
        )
    )


  percentage_data <-
    percentage_data %>%

    left_join(
      percentage_positions,
      by = ".category"
    )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Plot
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = .x,
      y = .y,
      color = .category
    )
  ) +

    # Variants
    geom_point(
      alpha = 0.6,
      size = 1
    ) +

    # FDR threshold
    geom_hline(
      yintercept =
        fdr_y,
      linetype =
        "dashed",
      linewidth =
        0.5
    ) +

    # Strongly detrimental threshold
    geom_vline(
      xintercept =
        strong_threshold,
      linetype =
        "dashed",
      linewidth =
        0.5
    ) +

    # WT/reference replication score
    geom_vline(
      xintercept =
        reference_value,
      linetype =
        "dashed",
      linewidth =
        0.5
    ) +

    # Percentages
    geom_text(
      data =
        percentage_data,

      aes(
        x = label_x,
        y = label_y,
        label = label
      ),

      inherit.aes =
        FALSE,

      color =
        "black",

      fontface =
        "bold",

      size =
        3
    ) +

    scale_color_manual(
      values =
        replication_category_colors,

      limits =
        replication_category_levels,

      drop =
        FALSE
    ) +

    coord_cartesian(
      xlim =
        x_lim,

      ylim =
        y_lim
    ) +

    labs(
      x =
        "Normalized replication score",

      y =
        expression(
          -log[10](FDR)
        ),

      title =
        plot_title,

      color =
        "Mutational effect"
    ) +

    theme_classic() +

    theme(
      plot.title =
        element_text(),

      legend.title =
        element_text(
          face = "bold"
        )
    )
}


# Volcano plot - all variants
volcano_plot_all <-
  plot_volcano(
    data =
      phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat,

    x_col =
      "fitness_final",

    y_col =
      "p_value_two_sample_ttest_syn_FDR",

    color_col =
      "mutation_category_FDR_lethal",

    x_lim =
      c(-1, 1.5),

    y_lim =
      c(0, 2.7),

    reference_value =
      1,

    strong_effect_cutoff =
      0.5,

    plot_title =
      "All variants, n=44,195"
  )

volcano_plot_all

#ggsave(volcano_plot_all, filename = "./plots/volcano_plot_all.pdf", width = 5, height = 3)


# Volcano plot - 1nt variants

  plot_volcano(
    data =
      phix_all_dms_sub_libraries_normalized_unique_stat_1nt,

    x_col =
      "fitness_final",

    y_col =
      "p_value_1nt_two_sample_ttest_syn_FDR",

    color_col =
      "mutation_category_FDR_lethal_1nt",

    x_lim =
      c(-1, 1.5),

    y_lim =
      c(0, 2.7),

    reference_value =
      1,

    strong_effect_cutoff =
      0.5,

    plot_title =
      "Single-nucleotide (1nt) variants, n=16,098"
  )

volcano_plot_1nt
```
